master.title: Acoustic Sensor Array Topologies for Partial Discharge Localisation in Electric Machines
master.content:
Increasing the reliability of electric machines is paramount for various industrial applications. In particular, for advanced electric propulsion systems being developed for electric vehicles, aircraft, and ships, which incorporate high power and high torque density electric machines. Insulation failure is reported to be responsible for up to 66% of machine breakdowns and proves to be one of the most challenging areas to develop condition based monitoring methods. A major indicator of electrical insulation breakdown is the occurrence of partial discharge events. This paper presents a method for localising partial discharge emissions using acoustic sensor arrays and a cross-correlation based time-difference of arrival algorithm. The results from analytical experiments are reported for a large traction based switched reluctance machine which demonstrates the effectiveness of the approach with accuracy errors of less than 1 cm Euclidean distance. This work serves as a valuable precursor towards developing future experiments with hardware.


Authors: Chelmiah E.T., Kavanagh D.F..

Affiliations: South East Technological University.

Publication: 2022 International Conference on Electrical Machines, ICEM 2022, 2022, pp.1582-1588.

candidate.title: Flux Switching Machines-for All-Electric Aircraft Applications
candidate.content:
The demand for new and efficient design of electric motors is gaining momentum due to the rapid growth in electric transportation. In particular, all-electric aircraft applications require very high-power density. This paper introduces new motor topologies for a double-rotor flux switching machine with an air-core stator comprising field and armature windings. The field coils are made of yttrium barium copper oxide high temperature superconducting material and aluminum Litz is used for the armature windings. The machine is operated under cryogenic temperatures. The power density obtained with the proposed design is 30.5 kW/kg and an efficiency is 95.2% during take-off is accomplished; satisfying the requirement of electric aviation.


Authors: Saeidabadi S., Kovacs C., Usman A., Haugan T.J., Corzine K., Parsa L..

Affiliations: University of California, Santa Cruz, Air Force Research Laboratory, Founder Scintillating Solutions LLC,Columbus 3.

Publication: 2022 International Conference on Electrical Machines, ICEM 2022, 2022, pp.1430-1436.
